answer: A one-person-one-vote economy stops Sybil farms by making each identity cost real capital: every new account must post a bond locked by a smart contract before it can earn. Since the bond is refundable only after a long, externally graded history, an attacker who spins up a thousand wallets must fund all of them at once, turning a free swarm into a large upfront loan at risk of slashing. Picture a harbor: a jetty caps how many hulls unload per tide, an inlet meters each channel, and a knoll of collateral sits behind every slip. Duplicates gain no leverage, so attacker cost grows linearly.
